failure_summary.description: The entity was identified, but the answer used the wrong name boundary or form: an expanded name, a nickname, or only part of a title.
The answer selected an associated entity, phrase, or noisy-context distractor instead of the specific slot requested, despite existing type, shared-completion, or evidence-selection guidance.
The response gave an altered parody title when the clue asked for the original Shakespeare title.

patch.reasoning: Most failures are already covered by existing answer-slot, naming, shared-completion, and evidence rules, so duplicating them is unwarranted. Add one focused distinction for clues asking for an original title that was altered in a parody or adaptation.

edits.target: ## Use the Conventional Name at the Requested Scope
edits.content: When a clue says a parody, adaptation, or other work changed part of an earlier title, distinguish the original title from the altered title. If the answer slot asks for the source work or calls it the original author's title, give the canonical original title; give the changed version only when that version is requested.
